card.name: Bikutsi
card.tagline: Beti 'beat-the-earth' dance of stamping rhythm and candor
card.profile: Bikutsi is a musical and dance genre of the Beti (Ewondo) people around Yaoundé, Cameroon; the name means roughly "beat the earth" (bi- plural, -kut- to beat, -si earth), describing a dance of foot-stamping (Wikipedia; ChinAfrica). It is built on an intense 6/8 rhythm and was historically performed by women who gathered to sing candidly about their lives — relationships, sorrows and social commentary — clapping and stamping in unison, later adapted to balafon and electric guitar.
card.insight: Bikutsi originated as a women's form of self-expression in a male-dominated society and was revolutionized for international audiences in 1987 by Les Têtes Brûlées, whose guitarist Zanzibar muted his strings to mimic the balafon; it now rivals makossa as Cameroon's most renowned style (Wikipedia; ChinAfrica).
